newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Australian Broadcasting Corp Morning Update.
newsitem.headline: Australian Broadcasting Corp Morning Update.

text.p: A top-level ACTU meeting in Newcastle over the next three days will give the union movement the chance to highlight the wrong it believes BHP has delivered to the town's workers. The closure of BHP's Newcastle steel making facilities will be one of the topics on the table during the ACTU's executive meeting. Senior executive members will address workers attending a rally during the national stoppage of BHP's national steel division on Thursday. Also up for discussion is the future of the ACTU's wage claim, and budget reaction.

There's been a call for a ban on imported cooked chicken meat into Australia. New South Wales Environment Minister, Pam Allen, wants the Federal Government to scrap a plan to allow the cooked chicken meat into Australia, because of the possible introduction of Newcastle disease, which can kill poultry and native bird species. The Minister says Newcastle disease has reached Australia on two occasions, including once in the 1930's when thousands of chickens died.

Police in the Northen Territory have confirmed the coroner has asked them to investigate the death of a 56-year-old woman, who died in April after a four-day drug-induced coma. Northern Territory Attorney General says he has no role in the investigation into the death of Esther Wild, who was denied use of the voluntary euthanasia law. Ms Wild had fulfilled the requirements of the right to die law, known as ROTI, but couldn't use it after the law was overridden by the Federal parliament. Mr Burke says it's the role of the coroner to be satisfied as to the cause of death of someone.

Despite heated exchanges between students and police, full fees for some Monash University students look likely to go ahead. Mounted police and about 20 officers on foot, clashed with protesters at the Clayton campus, using force to push through a student barricade. Inside, members of the Monash University council voted to defer their decision on fees until another meeting in July. Vice Chancellor David Robinson won't say when fees will be introduced, but admits they're inevitable. - - - -

Fourteen people remain stranded on Broughton Island off Port Stephens today, with heavy seas and gale force winds preventing them from returning to the mainland. A rescue helicopter was called to the island yesterday to replenish food supplies and deliver medication.
